The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click BillSubscriptionTracker.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on adding bills, ticking them off, renewals and backups.
  4. Add your bills: rent, utilities, insurance, phone, streaming. The usual ones are one click away on an empty app.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on the welcome screen or in Settings & backup. A fictional household’s 19 bills fill every screen, in a separate session. Return to my bills brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

What’s left to pay, at a glance.

Bill & Subscription Tracker answers one question first: how much is still to pay this month?

This month. The big number is what you haven’t ticked off yet; the ring shows what your bills cost a month, by category.

WordWhat it means
Every monthAll your bills averaged to one month: a yearly $120 bill counts as $10.
Left to payThis month’s bills not ticked off yet.
AutopayCounts as paid on its due day, without a tick.
Set asideYour yearly and quarterly bills ÷ 12: save this each month and they never surprise you.

Adding bills

Add each bill once.

Bills & subscriptions → Add a bill. Every later due date follows from the one you enter.

FieldWhat to enter
Name and amount“Electric”, “Netflix”. Amounts like $1,450 or 15.49 are fine.
Bill or subscriptionSubscriptions are counted apart, so you can see what they add up to.
How oftenEvery week, 2 weeks, month, 2 months, 3 months, 6 months, year, or once. A bill on the 31st falls on the last day of shorter months.
Next due dateThe next time it’s due. The calendar fills in from there.
On autopayIt ticks itself on its due day.
The amount changesFor electric or water: you’re asked what you really paid when you tick it.
Free trial endsNothing is due until then; the first charge is that day. You’re warned a week before.
Remind me to cancel byAny bill can have a reminder date.
Pays from, website, notesOptional: which card or account, the login page, an account number ending.

Price went up?

Edit the bill, type the new amount and the date it starts. Past months keep the old price, and the rise shows on Renewals & trials.

Each month

Tick them off.

This month lists every bill due, oldest first. Tick each one as you pay it.

Needs your attention

Overdue bills, bills due today, trials ending, cancel-by reminders and price rises appear at the top of This month, each with its button.

Skip, pause, cancel

Open a bill’s payment to Skip this one (a waived fee). Set a bill to Paused or Cancelled with a date: nothing is due after it, and cancelled ones count what you save.

Ticked something by mistake? Tick it again to take it back, or use Undo on the message at the bottom.

Read this one

Keeping your bills safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every bill, subscription, payment and category. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
A bill shows on the wrong dayEdit it and set the first due date; every later date follows from it.
An autopay bill didn’t go throughClick its tick to take it back, then mark it paid when it does.
A trial shows a chargeCheck the trial end date on the bill. The first charge is due that day.
Last month’s numbers changedA new price needs a start date; otherwise it applies from the first due date.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
